newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE'S AGRICULTURAL BANK RE-NEGOTIATES LOANS.
newsitem.headline: GREECE'S AGRICULTURAL BANK RE-NEGOTIATES LOANS.

text.p: The Agricultural Bank of Greece has stepped up its efforts to re-negotiate overdue loans to the Greek agricultural sector.
"The Agricultural Bank of Greece has rescheduled loans totalling 27 billion drachmas granted to farmers and agro-businesses by end-March 1997," the bank said in a statement.
Loans amounting to 10.9 billion drachmas were re-negotiated in March 1997.
It was part of a broader loan rescheduling programme which started a year earlier pursuant to the central bank's 1620 directive.
The bank dropped the collection of penalty interest on all overdue loans while also offering large discounts on overdue interest.
Increased demand from the bank's clientele to settle overdue loans may result in a two- or three-month extension in the loan rescheduling programme which officially ends April 1997.
Agricultural Bank sources said it is hoped that the loan rescheduling total will rise to as high as 50 billion drachmas.
The bank had dealt with 12,841 loan rescheduling cases until March 1997. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
